subject: GPA, PCA, and mshape scaling factor

messages.author: 7096219effdf1b81
messages.subject: GPA, PCA, and mshape scaling factor
parts:
Hi All,

I have a question about mean shape, scaling factors, and plotting a PCA. My analysis has multiple species with between 1-15 images per species and I’ve used tpsdig to landmark (both fixed and sliding). I want to plot a PCA using the mean shape of each species. I understand that there are two ways I could do this – the first being completing GPA on the entire dataset and then calculating the mean shape for each species to plot the PCA, and I know how to use coords.subset to accomplish this. 

But, from a theoretical perspective, there is a strong argument to be made for giving each species equal weighting in the GPA and so I also want to compare the results from above to results when the GPA is run separately for each species, the mean for each species is calculated, and then another GPA is completed on the mean shapes for all species before plotting the PCA. When using mshape, I know the average landmark position is returned, but it isn’t clear to me if a scaling factor is still present. So, my question is whether the scaling factor be lost after taking the mean shape for each species and whether the second GPA is still able to standardize for size differences? Or am I limited to the first method outlined above given there are substantial differences in size between my species.

 

Thanks,

Sara

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] GPA, PCA, and mshape scaling factor
parts:
Sara,
there is no scaling in mshape() as a function (extracting the consensus from the gpa result is a different story, although for your first approach they will arrive at the same place). mshape() just calculates an arithmetic average of landmark coordinates.

Hope this helps
Antigoni

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: GPA, PCA, and mshape scaling factor
parts: Since you have sample imbalances across your species, and you want your PCA shape not to be biased towards species with more samples, an easier solution would be fitting GPA (without scaling) for each species individually, and feeding the consensus shapes from those into your final shape analysis and PCA decomposition. In your final analysis, by definition each species (with multiple samples) will be represented by their species means.
